author: OpenTikZ contributors
description: FlashAttention, three-panel homage after Dao et al., 2022. Left: the GPU memory hierarchy as a banded triangle (SRAM 19 TB/s / HBM 1.5 TB/s / DRAM 12.8 GB/s) showing the bandwidth-vs-size trade-off. Center: the IO-aware dataflow — Q, K^T and V tiles streamed from HBM, copied block-by-block into SRAM (outer loop over K/V, inner loop over Q), where the QK^T block and softmax are fused before sm(QK^T)V is written back to HBM. Right: the GPT-2 attention runtime, a stacked PyTorch bar (Matmul/Mask/Softmax/Dropout/Matmul) versus FlashAttention's single fused kernel.
name: FlashAttention (IO-aware attention)

author: OpenTikZ contributors
description: Block-level GAN overview: a low-dimensional latent bar feeds the generator G (expanding trapezoid) producing generated fake images, while a high-dimensional sample-space stack supplies real images; both feed the discriminator D (compressing trapezoid) that outputs a real/fake decision. Parametric sizes, colors, and labels.
name: Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)

author: OpenTikZ contributors
description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA), two-panel homage after Hu et al., 2021. During training: a frozen pretrained weight W feeds Wx in parallel with a trainable low-rank update B·A (rank-r bottleneck, A=N(0,sigma^2), B=0) feeding BAx, summed to h. After training: the adapter is folded into a single merged weight matrix W_merged, shown as a bar–square–bar stack. Center column gives h = Wx + BAx = (W + BA)x.
name: LoRA (low-rank adaptation)

the inter-tile bus is always dashed and the intra-tile bus is always solid — this distinction is load-bearing (NoC/global vs. local/tile-internal), grafted from tikzsetup.tex's intrabus/interbus split

author: cp-4892 (WP-4, ADR-0005 D5) -- extends the esl-crossbar-kcl PoC (cp-4856) with a \foreach-driven array generator
description: Parametric nrows x ncols VMM crossbar-cell array (contract §1a `crossbar-array`), generated by nested \foreach loops with row/col-indexed node names, row voltage sources, and per-column KCL summation nodes. Wiring uses O(1)-per-row/column rails (a single colinear draw through every cell in the line), not O(rows*cols) point-to-point wires, so the array stays both correct-looking and legible at scale. Proven at 64x64 with celllabelmode=none (blank cell fill) and edgelabelstride (only every Nth row/col index annotated) as the explicit legibility rules. Colors reuse the esl-crossbar-kcl domain-semantic scheme (blue=input/activation, green=analog weight cell, orange=analog current/summation).

invariants: row/column wiring is drawn as ONE colinear rail per row (vin-<r> through cell-<r>-<ncols>) and ONE colinear rail per column (cell-1-<c> through cell-<nrows>-<c> or kcl-<c>) -- never point-to-point per cell, which would be both O(rows*cols) edges and a visually incorrect crossbar reading at scale

above roughly 10x10-15x15 cells, set \celllabelmode to "none" and raise \edgelabelstride -- per-cell subscript text and a numeric label on every row/column both collide or become unreadable at higher densities; verified by rendering to PNG before shipping any array this size (ADR-0005 D6). Cell identity/addressability never depends on the printed label, only on the node name
the two-index node-naming stays row-then-col and 1-based at any array size: cell-<r>-<c>, never renumbered or collapsed when the array resizes

colors encode role/domain semantics (cell=weight, vsource/vwire=input, kclnode/awire=analog-current), not decoration -- do not introduce a color not tied to a role, and do not reuse opentikz's ot* palette names for these roles (palette collision, see cp-4856 learnings note)
edit_contract.node_naming: generated, index-addressable, 1:1 with contract §1a: cell-<r>-<c> is a crossbar-cell (contract component `crossbar-cell`), 1-based row,col over the \nrows x \ncols array -- together the array IS the contract's `crossbar-array` ("a full nrows x ncols VMM cell array, placed by row/col index"); vin-<r> is a v-source (contract component `v-source`), 1-based row index; kcl-<c> is a kcl-node (contract component `kcl-node`), 1-based column index, present only when \showkcl=1. This replaces esl-crossbar-kcl's fixed concatenated-digit naming (g11, g21, ...), which is ambiguous once row or col exceeds 9 -- coordinate with the WP-2 adapter's node_naming derivation (cp-4890) on which scheme becomes the family-wide convention before both templates diverge permanently.

operations.summary: edit \nrows/\ncols -- the generator re-derives every node name, rail, and KCL node; no coordinate ever needs hand-editing
set \celllabelmode to "none" once the array is large enough that per-cell $G_{r,c}$ text would collide (see invariants); the cell's identity is still its node name, not its printed text
set \showkcl to 0 to omit the per-column summation node while keeping the column rail (e.g. when only the array structure matters, not the readout stage)
raise \edgelabelstride so only every Nth row/col gets an index annotation at the array's edge -- the first and last row/col are always labeled regardless of stride

as in esl-crossbar-kcl: declare a coordinate below a kcl-<c> node and draw a real circuitikz `to[...]` bipole to it -- this generator does not itself draw readout devices, it only produces the array + rails + KCL nodes for a downstream circuit template (WP-5) to attach them to

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role (cell/vsource/kclnode/awire/vwire) in that role's style definition; keep the esl-crossbar-kcl assignments (green=cell, blue=vsource/vwire, orange=kclnode/awire) unless a family settled-decisions record overrides it

parameters.meaning: number of crossbar rows (VMM input rows)
parameters.name: \nrows

parameters.meaning: number of crossbar columns (VMM output columns)
parameters.name: \ncols

parameters.meaning: "full" prints $G_{r,c}$ inside each cell; "none" leaves cells blank -- the legibility control for large arrays
parameters.name: \celllabelmode

parameters.meaning: 1 draws a per-column KCL summation node terminating the column rail; 0 omits it (the column rail still connects every cell in the column)
parameters.name: \showkcl

parameters.meaning: show a row/col index label only every Nth line (plus the first and last, always); 1 = label every line -- the legibility control for row/col axis annotation at large nrows/ncols
parameters.name: \edgelabelstride

author: cp-4856 PoC graft (grounded in analog-ai EmbML-HB-2026-Ch-AnalogEDAI/fig/figstyle.tex, not a fork of that file)
description: Analog in-memory-compute crossbar readout: 2x2 weight-cell array driven by row voltage sources, per-column KCL summation (Sigma) nodes, and a real circuitikz device-symbol readout stage (sense resistor / reference current source) per column. First circuitikz-based template in this local checkout -- opentikz ships zero circuitikz coverage upstream. Colors are the analog-ai domain-semantic scheme (blue=input/activation, green=analog weight cell, orange=analog current/summation), grafted from figstyle.tex, not opentikz's five-color ot* palette (see cp-4856 learnings note on the palette-invariant collision).

invariants: two-index subscripts stay comma-separated ($G_{i,j}$, $I_{i,j}$), never $G_{ij}$ -- family-wide convention from figstyle.tex/adcbuffer.tex

circuitikz `to[...]` bipoles are reserved for real EE devices (resistor/source/capacitor/etc.); crossbar cells, KCL nodes, and voltage-source glyphs stay the hand-styled figstyle node styles (cell/kclnode/vsource) -- do not redraw a cell as a circuitikz bipole, and do not redraw a real device as a plain tikz node; mixing the two idioms in one figure is intentional here and must stay legible (label each readout branch, as in operations.add-readout-device)

awire (orange, analog current) is reserved for cell-to-KCL-node and KCL-node-to-device wiring; vwire (blue) is reserved for source-to-cell wiring; never swap wire colors across the analog/digital or voltage/current domain boundary

every KCL node must have a labeled incoming-current annotation (currentlbl) placed clear of neighboring columns -- verify by rendering to PNG before committing; label collisions between adjacent columns are the primary failure mode this template hit during the cp-4856 PoC (fixed via xshift offsets on the readout captions)

the visual self-check (pdftoppm -> read the PNG) is mandatory before calling this template done -- this exact template shipped with two colliding label pairs on first compile and only the render caught it
edit_contract.node_naming: fixed semantic node names: (v<row>) row voltage sources, (g<row><col>) crossbar cells (e.g. g11, g21), (k<col>) per-column KCL nodes, (k<col>out) readout-branch coordinate; new rows/columns extend the same <row>/<col> integer-suffix scheme -- this PoC hand-instantiates a fixed 2x2 array rather than a \foreach loop (see operations.add-row / add-column for what a real edit does)

operations.summary: edit the matching label macro, or the literal $G_{i,j}$/$I_{i,j}$ text in a cell/current-label node (kept literal, not macro-driven, to preserve the family's comma-separated two-index subscript convention -- see invariants)

add \node[vsource] (v3) at (0,-2*\rowgap) {...}; add a \node[cell] (g3<c>) per existing column at the same x as g1<c>/g2<c>, y=-2*\rowgap; wire \draw[vwire] (v3) -- (g3<c>); and \draw[awire] (g3<c>) -- (k<c>); for every column

add a \node[cell] (g<r>3) per existing row at x=3*\colgap; wire \draw[vwire] (v<r>) -- (g<r>3); add a \node[kclnode] (k3) below the new column; wire every \draw[awire] (g<r>3) -- (k3); and its readout branch (see add-readout-device)

declare \coordinate (k<c>out) at ($(k<c>)+(0,-1.15)$); then \draw (k<c>) to[<device>, l=$<label>$, o-o] (k<c>out); -- <device> is a real circuitikz bipole key (R, I, C, L, ...), NOT a figstyle node style; this is the one place this template mixes circuitikz bipoles with hand-styled tikzset nodes

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role in that role's style definition; keep vsource=blue, cell=green, kclnode/awire/currentlbl=orange, per the analog-ai family's settled scheme, unless a project's own settled-decisions record overrides it (this template ships no settled-decisions record of its own -- it is a PoC graft, not the shipped Phase-1 component library, see D4/R2.3 of ADR-0004)

author: cp-4892 (WP-4, ADR-0005 D5) -- extends the esl-architecture-block PoC (cp-4856) with a \foreach-driven array generator
description: Parametric MPSoC tile grid (\ntilerows x \ntilecols) with a PE sub-grid (\pegridrows x \pegridcols) contained inside each tile, generated by nested \foreach loops rather than hand-listed nodes. Node names stay index-addressable (tile-<r>-<c>, pe-<r>-<c>-<k>) at any scale. Proven at 32+ tiles with legibility handled via pelabelmode (blank PE fill above a few tiles) and an O(tiles) inter-tile mesh (not O(tiles^2)). Colors reuse the esl-architecture-block domain-semantic scheme (Aquamarine=PE/core-accent, Orange=intra-bus, NavyBlue dashed=inter-bus).

invariants: each tile's fit box is declared after every PE node it fits, inside an on-background-layer scope, so it sits behind them (containment primitive, §3a)
node names stay index-addressable at any grid size: tile-<r>-<c> and pe-<r>-<c>-<k>, never renumbered or collapsed when the grid resizes

the inter-tile mesh only wires each tile to its immediate right/below neighbor (O(tiles) edges) -- never a full mesh (O(tiles^2)), which is both semantically wrong for a NoC and illegible past a handful of tiles

above roughly 8-12 tiles, set \pelabelmode to "none" -- per-PE numeric text at that density collides or becomes unreadable; verified by rendering to PNG before shipping any array this size (ADR-0005 D6). PE identity/addressability never depends on the printed label, only on the node name

colors encode role/domain semantics (pe=core-accent, intrabus, interbus), not decoration -- do not introduce a color not tied to a role, and do not reuse opentikz's ot* palette names for these roles (palette collision, see cp-4856 learnings note)
edit_contract.node_naming: generated, index-addressable, 1:1 with contract §1b: tile-<r>-<c> is the tile/cluster container (contract component `tile`), 1-based row,col over the \ntilerows x \ntilecols grid; pe-<r>-<c>-<k> is a processing element (contract component `pe`) inside tile (r,c), 1-based flat index k (row-major) over that tile's \pegridrows x \pegridcols sub-grid. This extends esl-architecture-block's fixed "role+tile-index" naming (core1, acc1, ...) to full 2-D grid addressing so the same array-scale node can be targeted by (row,col[,k]) rather than a single flat suffix -- coordinate with the WP-2 adapter's node_naming derivation (cp-4890) before treating this as the family-wide convention.

set \pelabelmode to "none" once the grid is large enough that per-PE index text would collide (see invariants); the PE's identity is still its node name, not its printed text
set \showmesh to 0 to omit the inter-tile NoC mesh entirely (e.g. when only containment/tile-array structure matters, not interconnect)
\pesize/\pegap for PE sizing and intra-tile density; \tilegapx/\tilegapy for inter-tile density

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role (pe/tilebox/intrabus/interbus) in that role's style definition; keep the esl-architecture-block assignments (Aquamarine=PE, Orange=intrabus, NavyBlue-dashed=interbus) unless a family settled-decisions record overrides it
